info.title: compy
info.description: Local OpenTelemetry Collector manager: REST API served by whatever UI process is running (compy ui / window / tray). Localhost-only; see internal/webui's host-check + CSRF middleware.

still_running.description: Present when an activation failed and the previous configuration was put back, e.g. "otlp-to-bronto · staging".

protocol.description: The advertised OTLP protocol; endpoint points at the port it uses (the gRPC port for grpc, the HTTP port otherwise).

recent.description: The most recently activated configurations, newest first.

listening.description: TCP ports the collector process is actually listening on, detected from the OS (launchd pid + lsof), sorted ascending. Absent when stopped or undetectable — never derived from settings or YAML.

conformance.description: Whether an app following compy's advertised endpoint would reach the running collector. Absent when stopped or when port detection is unavailable — no detection, no claim.

compy_version.description: The running compy build itself, as displayed: "0.1.0" for a release, "dev · <12-char revision>" (+dirty when built from a modified tree) for a dev build, "unknown" without build info.

compy_update.description: A newer compy release the background check knows of (e.g. "0.2.0"). Present only on release builds with a strictly newer release known — a dev build never claims.

stale_binary.description: Present (true) when the installed LaunchAgent names a collector binary that no longer exists — what `brew upgrade` leaves behind. A running collector survives on the deleted inode but any launchd restart would fail; restarting through compy re-resolves the binary and heals it.

PortsVerdict.description: The advertised-ports verdict. conforming rides on the primary port alone — the port OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT actually uses under the advertised protocol (the HTTP port for http/protobuf and http/json, the gRPC port for grpc); the other port missing is reported but never fails the verdict by itself.

missing_http.description: The advertised HTTP port is not among the detected listeners (a softer addendum when the advertised protocol is grpc).

missing_grpc.description: The advertised gRPC port is not among the detected listeners (a softer addendum unless the advertised protocol is grpc).

actual.description: Detected non-telemetry listeners — the ports POST /api/service/adopt-ports would adopt.

SettingsUpdate.description: Partial: an absent field leaves that setting unchanged. Port changes take effect on next apply; a protocol change is advertisement-only and needs no restart.

protocol.description: What the advertised endpoint speaks. Any other value is a 400.

modified.description: The config's content hash differs from its pristine hash. For a templated (tier-3) config the SOURCE carries the hash — it IS the config.

has_template.description: True for a tier-3 configuration: a template source (config.tmpl) exists that the yaml is rendered from. GET /api/configs/{name} returns it as "source".

presets.description: One value bag per preset — a preset holds ALL of a config's values. Tier 2: env strings keyed by variable name. Tier 3: typed schema values keyed by field name (plus "backends": an array of per-row objects), secrets included as strings.

source.description: The template source (schema front matter — YAML between "---" marker lines, or the original JSON form — + "---" + body), present only when info.has_template is true. The yaml is its rendered output.

template.description: The parsed schema of the source, present when the config has a source and it parses — what the editor's form is generated from (the client never parses front matter itself).

version.description: The INSTALLED version: a downloaded definition's version in effect (compiled-in pin or pulled update), the bundled collector's build stamp ("unknown" when the stamp file is missing). Empty for user-managed entries, for the bundled collector when it is not built, and for undownloaded definitions (nothing is installed — see fetch_version for what a download would fetch).

bundled.description: True for the collector shipped with compy (otelcol-compy, resolved next to the compy executable, never downloaded — it updates with compy releases), unless a user entry overrides the name.

user_entry.description: True iff this name has an actual entry in the user distro registry (distros.json) — a custom distro, or an override of a shipped definition's path. False for a shipped definition that's merely been downloaded to its default path: there's no registry entry for DELETE /api/distros/{name} to remove.

download.description: Present only while a download of this distro is in flight in the serving process — including one an activation started automatically (the default collector fetched on first need), so the settings screen's periodic refresh can show a progress bar for a download it did not start.

latest_available.description: The newest upstream release, present only when it is newer than this row's INSTALLED version, per the persisted release check (the tray's ~12h background check, or an on-demand GET /api/distros/{name}/update — both record the same result). Read from disk, never fetched during this request. Only on installed updatable rows: never on an undownloaded definition (nothing exists to update — its first download fetches the newest release directly), the bundled collector (it updates with compy releases), or user-managed entries, and a malformed/unknown current version never claims.

fetch_version.description: What a download of this row would fetch: the newest release the persisted check knows, or the compiled-in pin when no check has run yet (fetch_pinned). Only on undownloaded, platform-available definitions.

fetch_pinned.description: Present (true) when fetch_version is the compiled-in pin because no release check result exists yet, rather than a checked latest release.

checked_at.description: When the persisted release check last succeeded (a failed check keeps the previous result and its checked_at rather than claim staleness away). Absent until a check has succeeded; only on updatable rows, like latest_available.

port.description: The localhost port whose /metrics answered this scrape. Absent when unavailable.

dropping.description: The drop diagnosis: present only when the running collector reports dropped > 0 AND the active configuration's effective preset is missing required values (cfgstore.MissingRequired — no ${VAR:-fallback} in the yaml, not COMPY_*, empty in the preset). Drops with all values present carry no diagnosis: some other cause, no vars blamed.

TemplateField.description: One form input in a template schema. Array order IS form order.

default.description: String for slug/url/string/choice, boolean for toggle, array of strings for multi. A secret never has one. Absent means required (unless optional).

section.description: The section id this field renders under.

advanced.description: Per-repeat-row disclosure: hidden behind "more options", always with a common-case-correct default.

Template.description: One catalog entry: enough schema for the creation form to render itself. A `secret` field takes no knob value — it renders as a ${env:...} reference whose value lives in presets.

collapsed.description: A collapsed section is safely ignorable: every field in it defaults to the common case.

backends.description: The repeat group: min..max rows of fields. Knob shape: {"backends": [{...}, ...]}.

Knobs.description: Initial values for a config created from a catalog entry, keyed by field name (plus "backends": an array of per-row objects when the template has a repeat group); they seed the fresh default preset, which owns ALL of the config's values. Values: string for slug/url/string/choice/secret, boolean for toggle, array of strings for multi. Omitted fields take their schema default; a non-secret field with neither value nor default is a 400 naming the field, as is an unknown field.

get.summary: The collector's own metrics, scraped from its telemetry endpoint
get.description: Four numbers for the Collector screen. localhost:8888 (otelcol's default) is tried first; if it does not answer, the collector's detected listening ports are probed and the first parsable /metrics wins — `port` names the winner. A stopped or unscrapable collector answers 200 with available:false and zeroes, never an error. Sources (otelcol 0.135, counters matched with or without a _total suffix): received = otelcol_receiver_accepted_{spans,metric_points,log_records}; exported = otelcol_exporter_sent_{spans,metric_points,log_records}; queue = otelcol_exporter_queue_size; dropped = otelcol_receiver_refused_*, otelcol_exporter_send_failed_*, otelcol_exporter_enqueue_failed_*.

post.summary: Set the advertised grpc/http ports to the running config's actual OTLP listeners
post.description: The advertisement follows the deliberate config. With an empty body the detected non-telemetry listeners are classified (the otlp/http listener speaks HTTP/1.1, the grpc one does not); any ambiguity — no or several http-ish candidates, more candidates than slots — is refused with a 400 naming the candidates, never guessed silently. An explicit body resolves it: each given port must be one of the detected candidates. Applying goes through the same path as PUT /api/settings (OS-level env refreshed when on); shipped configs pick the new ports up on their next activation.

schema.description: Optional. Absent fields are classified (or, when the other is given, left unchanged).

400.description: Collector not running / nothing detected, classification ambiguous (candidates named in the message), or an explicit port that is not a detected listener

put.summary: Replace a configuration's YAML. A body carrying template front matter (JSON: '{' + "---" separator; or YAML between "---" marker lines whose content parses as a schema — a plain config merely opening with the "---" document marker stays plain) is tier-3 SOURCE and routes through the source save pipeline (parse, render, validate-or-restore); plain yaml written over a templated config demotes it to plain (the source is dropped).

parameters.name: validate
parameters.description: Pass "false" to write without asking the collector — the escape hatch for a config whose referenced variables have no values yet. The running collector is never touched: an unvalidated config is not auto-applied, so an active running configuration keeps its previous version until the next restart or activation (reported as running_stale: true).

running_stale.description: Only with validate=false: the active running collector kept the previous version of this config.

put.summary: Save a tier-3 configuration's template source. The source ONLY — preset values travel through the preset routes (a preset owns ALL of a config's values). The pipeline parses the schema, reconciles every preset's bag with it (unknown fields pruned, newly defaulted fields filled — per preset), re-renders from the active preset's bag, stores source + rendered yaml + reconciled presets, then validates the rendered config against the collector — a rejection restores everything (nothing was saved).

parameters.name: validate
parameters.description: Pass "false" to store without asking the collector — the same escape hatch as the yaml route's. The running collector is never touched; running_stale reports when the active running collector kept the previous version.

400.description: Bad request — an empty source, a source without front matter, a schema or body that does not parse, a render the active preset's bag cannot satisfy (the message names the field), or a rendered config the collector rejects (nothing was saved)

put.summary: Create or replace a whole preset's value bag. A preset owns ALL of a config's values: env strings for a tier-2 config; typed schema values (options, repeat groups, toggles, secrets) for a tier-3 one, validated against the schema (a 400 names the field) and proven against the collector BEFORE anything is stored (nothing-was-saved without a restore). Writing the config's active preset also refreshes the derived config.yaml and re-applies a running config.

parameters.name: validate
parameters.description: Pass "false" to skip the collector's verdict on a tier-3 bag (schema validation still applies) — the same escape hatch as the source route's. The running collector is never touched; running_stale reports when the active running collector kept a stale render. A tier-2 preset write never asked the collector, so the flag changes nothing there.

values.description: The preset's whole value bag. Tier 2: env strings keyed by variable name. Tier 3: schema values keyed by field name (plus "backends": an array of per-row objects); string for slug/url/string/choice/secret, boolean for toggle, array of strings for multi. Omitted fields take their schema default.

running_stale.description: Only with validate=false: the active running collector kept the previous render of this config.

400.description: Bad request — a malformed body, a tier-3 bag the schema rejects (the message names the field, e.g. backends[0].endpoint), or a render the collector rejects (nothing was saved)

get.summary: How this collector binary's download is going
get.description: Poll after POST .../fetch, which returns immediately. status is idle | downloading | done | failed; pct is 0-100 (and stays put when the server declares no Content-Length); error is present only when status is failed. Progress is per-process and in memory: a name nobody has fetched since this process started reads idle, whether or not the binary is on disk.

post.summary: Start downloading a shipped distro definition's binary (returns at once; poll .../progress)

200.description: Accepted — the download has started (or the binary was already present). Nothing else is reported here: an unknown name, a checksum mismatch or a network failure all surface through .../progress as status "failed", since this request is long gone by then.

get.summary: Check the latest upstream release for a pinned distro (core, contrib, otlp) — on demand, downloads nothing
get.description: The version in effect and the newest upstream release of open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases. A successful check is recorded in the state dir (the same record the tray's background check writes), so every distro row's latest_available/checked_at refreshes with it. 400 for the bundled collector (it updates with compy releases), a user-managed entry, an undownloaded distro (nothing installed to update — a download fetches the newest release directly), or an unknown name; a network failure or rate limit is an honest error, never a claim about versions.

400.description: Not updatable: the bundled collector, a user-managed entry, or an unknown name

502.description: The upstream release check failed: GitHub unreachable, rate-limited, or its answer unusable (e.g. a tag that is not a release version)

post.summary: Pull the latest upstream release of a pinned distro (returns at once when newer; poll .../progress)
post.description: Checks synchronously; started false with no error means already newest — the upstream answer is not strictly newer than the installed version (an equal or older answer is never a downgrade). Otherwise the tarball downloads in the background — verified against the .sha256 checksum asset published in the same upstream release — into its own versioned directory, becomes the version in effect, and, when this distro is the collector in use and the job is running, the service re-applies onto it (a new collector that fails to start rolls the update back with the last-good restore; a stopped collector stays stopped).

400.description: Not updatable: the bundled collector, a user-managed entry, or an unknown name

502.description: The upstream release check failed: GitHub unreachable, rate-limited, or its answer unusable (e.g. a tag that is not a release version)
